title: The Devotee Prince
logline: Harun al-Rashid's sixteen-year-old son gives up the palace for a wool robe and a bricklayer's wage in Basra, and dies unknown on bare earth with a royal ruby still unspent in his pocket.
moral: Rank and riches end in the same plain grave; the prince owned wealth and chose not to use it.
tone: Quiet, tender and dignified, with light warmth in the middle (the bird that snubs the caliph, the worker who refuses a raise). No jokes after the third Saturday; the death is gentle and shown without distress.

beats.summary: A caliph's son of sixteen, ill at ease among gold.
He visits graves and sees that rank does not mark them.
His father finds him in coarse wool; courtiers disapprove; he is scolded.
The bird he calls comes to his hand, and (50.52) refuses the caliph's.
He takes it as a sign and decides to leave Baghdad.
In Basra he lays bricks for one dirham and one daniq, stops for prayer, eats with the small coin and gives away the big one.
Abu Amir offers double pay; the worker pushes the extra back.
Third Saturday: the worker does not come.
He lies ill on bare earth with a brick for a pillow and makes two requests.
A precious ruby in the wool robe.
Harun recognises his wife's gift to their son.
Harun rides to the plain grave in Basra.
The unused ruby stays as a witness to wealth owned and never spent.

props.description: NEW brickWall(ctx, x0, x1, baseY, {courses:7, build:0..1, gap:0..1, seed}): running-bond clay bricks 60 x 28 with 4 mortar joints, red-brown #b5522d with red dot shading and black outline. build reveals bricks in laying order (left to right, bottom up); the newest brick drops 20 units with a squash. gap cuts a V-shaped hole (up to 4 bricks wide, 4 courses deep) that closes from the bottom as gap goes 1 to 0, with 5 loose bricks on the ground. A single brick(ctx, x, y, rot) is exported for the stack, the pillow and the hands.

Planned name (AN-095): plain grave. Here: earth mound 150 x 36 (half ellipse, ochre-brown, dot shading) with a rounded headstone 46 wide x 70 high at its left end; no inscription. fresh:true gives darker earth and three small clods.

Planned jewels (red cut gem): hexagonal brilliant, 44 wide x 38 high in the hand (drawn up to 3x in close shots), red #e2231a with a darker lower facet, white table highlight, black outline; used with the planned goldGlow tinted red.
Planned coinPile in its silver palette: single coins. Dirham r 26, daniq r 12, both off-white #e9e6dc with a grey rim line; a small heap of gold for the tray in S1 and inside the thought cloud.
Mason's trowel: diamond steel blade 46 x 26 (grey-white), short brown handle 30; held in the hand or lying on the wall.

Simple minaret: cream shaft 46 wide rising from behind the alley wall to y 240, balcony ring 80 wide at y 300, small blue dome and yellow finial on top. Should be the same drawing as the minaret of the planned mosqueCourt.
Planned small props under their planned names: purse, bread (round loaf r 22), waterJug, foodTray (tray for the coins in S1), crownProp (icon and in the hand), bindle, folded cloth.

subtitles.ar: كان للخليفة هارون الرشيد ابن بلغ السادسة عشرة،|لكنه لم يجد راحته في حياة القصور.|كان يزور المقابر كثيرًا|ويتأمل كيف انتهى أصحاب السلطان والمال إلى قبور لا يميزها جاه.
subtitles.en: Caliph Harun al-Rashid had a sixteen-year-old son|who was uneasy with palace life.|He visited graveyards|and reflected on how even rulers ended there.

subtitles.ar: مر هارون بابنه يومًا وهو يرتدي ثوبًا من الصوف.|رأى بعض الحاشية أن هيئته تسيء إلى مكانة الخليفة،|فعاتبه أبوه.|لكن الشاب أشار إلى طائر على سور القصر.
subtitles.en: One day Harun saw his son in coarse wool.|Courtiers considered the sight embarrassing,|and the caliph reproached him.|The youth pointed to a bird.

subtitles.ar: دعا الشاب الطائر فنزل على يده،|ثم طلب منه أن يقف على يد أبيه فلم يفعل.|تقول الحكاية إن الابن رأى في ذلك علامة،|وقرر ترك بغداد والعيش بعيدًا عن زخارف الحكم.
subtitles.en: The bird came to the prince’s hand|but refused his father’s,|according to the legend.|The youth decided to leave Baghdad and its riches.

subtitles.ar: وصل الأمير إلى البصرة وعمل في بناء الجدران.|كان يشترط أجرًا قليلًا: درهمًا ودانقًا،|ويطلب التوقف عند الأذان للصلاة مع الجماعة.|ينفق الدانق على طعامه ويتصدق بالدرهم.
subtitles.en: In Basra he worked building walls|for one dirham and one daniq,|pausing for communal prayers.|He ate with the daniq and gave the dirham as charity.

subtitles.ar: استأجره رجل اسمه أبو عامر لترميم جدار في بيته،|فأعجبه إتقانه وصيامه.|حاول أن يعطيه أجرًا مضاعفًا، لكن الشاب رفض الزيادة.|وعاد للعمل يوم السبت التالي بالشروط نفسها.
subtitles.en: A man named Abu Amir hired him to repair a wall|and admired his discipline.|He offered extra wages, but the young worker refused|and returned the following Saturday.

subtitles.ar: في السبت الثالث علم أبو عامر أن العامل مريض في كوخ قرب المقابر.|زاره فوجده مستلقيًا على الأرض، وقد جعل لبنة وسادة.|طلب الشاب أن يدفنه بعد موته،|ثم يسلم ما في جيب ثوبه إلى أبيه.
subtitles.en: On the third Saturday Abu Amir found the youth ill in a hut near the graves,|resting his head on a brick.|The youth asked him to bury him|and deliver something to his father.

subtitles.ar: مات الشاب كما توقع في الحكاية،|فغسله أبو عامر ودفنه.|وجد في ثوبه ياقوتة ثمينة، وحملها إلى بغداد.|وحين رآها هارون عرف أنها هدية سبق أن أعطتها الأم لابنها.
subtitles.en: The youth died.|Abu Amir buried him|and found a precious ruby sewn into his clothing.|In Baghdad Harun recognized it as a gift from the boy’s mother.

subtitles.ar: بكى هارون وأم الأمير عند سماع الخبر،|ثم سافر الخليفة مع أبي عامر إلى القبر في البصرة.|حزن الأب لأنه فقد ابنه،|وبقيت الياقوتة شاهدًا على مال امتلكه الشاب ولم يستخدمه.
subtitles.en: Both parents grieved.|Harun traveled to the grave in Basra with Abu Amir.|The unused ruby became a reminder|of the riches the prince had renounced.

owner_questions: The script says only "a bird"; default: a white dove, which also flies from the hut window at the death (129.9) and lands on the headstone at the end (an addition beyond the script).

The death is shown gently: eyes close, the hand slips, the lamp goes out; the washing is implied by a jug and a folded cloth and the burial by a finished mound (no body, no shroud shown). Default: keep it this soft.

Invented English lettering (20 items): THE DEVOTEE PRINCE, AGE 16, WOOL!, TWEET!, NOPE!, A SIGN, BAGHDAD, BASRA, 1 DIRHAM, 1 DANIQ, PRAYER TIME, CHARITY, ABU AMIR, FASTING, X2, NEXT SATURDAY, THIRD SATURDAY, RUBY!, FROM HIS MOTHER, THE END. Default: use all; NOPE! is the first to drop if the bird moment should stay serious.
The call to prayer is shown as sound arcs from a minaret and the youth walking off; the prayer itself is not depicted, and no adhan sound is synthesised. Default: keep it off screen.

Additions for clarity: a servant offering a tray of gold in S1, a beggar receiving the dirham in S8, a neighbour bringing the news in S11, and Abu Amir offering his cloak as a pillow in S13. Default: keep all four.
Harun al-Rashid and the queen are drawn as the generic caliph and lady figures, weeping with visible tears. Default: acceptable for named historical figures in this comic style.

Abu Amir uses the brick from the hut as the head marker of the grave (a visual echo, not in the script). Default: an ordinary headstone like the others, the brick left out, so that the grave is truly identical to the rest.
implementation_notes: All cue times are the word starts in planning/inputs/timeline.md; build CUE with w(p, n) from timing.json and do not hard-code if the indices are available. Paragraph and word indices used are in each action's cue.
Set LIFE.t = t every frame so every figure blinks; give explicit lid only where listed. Every character has a gaze target at all times (lookAt).
The prince changes costume once: costume "prince" in S1 and S2 (crown in hand in S2), "devotee" from S3 to the end. Sick: lighten the skin tone slightly and use lid 0.45 to 0.7.

Walks: Object.assign(P, walk(xf, t)) with footfalls for dust; riders with rideOn and GAIT strides. The track shots on desertRoad use camX with ctx.translate(-camX, 0) and the front pass (lip) after the cast.
brickWall is the visual clock of the middle act: build 0.35 to 0.5 in S7, the gap closing 1 to 0.35 in S9, 0.35 to 0.15 in S10, and frozen at 0.15 with the idle trowel in S11.
Thought cloud in S2: thoughtCloud(ctx, 680, 420, 420, 300, t, {inside}) with the figures at scale 0.5 so they stay over 110 px on screen.
The counter box for the wage (S7, S8, S10) is one function: box at panel top, big coin left, small coin right, each with its label; coins leave it by arcs.

Lettering lives in the top band of the panel or beside props; never across a face. Balloons with icons (crown, lying figure, grave, crowned head) are plain white boxes with a tail, icons 60 to 90 units.

Sound: six effects only, all in pauses: 5.74 chime (AGE 16 settles), 21.2 soft thud (crown set down), 36.02 chirp, 62.6 whoosh (LATER card), 166.48 soft chime (ruby revealed in the palm), 173.9 chime (THE END). master 0.6, each quieter than the voice.
The one LATER transition is at 62.0 to 63.6 (the 1.18 s pause). The Saturday jumps use labels and a sky sweep, not a second card.
Film length 177.42 s (173.42 + 4.0 hold), under the 180 s limit.
warnings: The narration has only three real pauses (5.36, 20.72, 62.04) plus two short gaps (35.76, 166.27); keep sound effects to the six listed.
S12 (hut exterior, 2.4 s) and S16 (ride to Baghdad, 2.6 s) are very short: keep them to one clear motion each.
villageYard has a forest backdrop; for a Basra house it may read too rural. Check a still; if so swap the backdrop for townFarCity or use marketStreet with one house front.
The palace battlement height for the bird is read from the catalogue image (approximate); measure it on the marketStreet anchors.

P8 English is shorter than the Arabic (the father's grief sentence is folded into "Both parents grieved"), so English chunk 3 appears while the Arabic says "the father grieved because he lost his son"; this is a chunk alignment compromise, the text is verbatim.
The devotee preset must be clean-shaven and read as a youth at phone size; keep the skull cap small so he is not confused with the villagers.
